subject: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@skyloftmedia.com>, Priya Agarwal <pri@skyloftmedia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for production inference. We want to make the observability onboarding as low-friction as possible. I put together a short kickoff itinerary and a handful of artifacts (attached) we use for typical implementations: dashboard templates, a runbook scaffold, and a one-page timeline.

Top-level asks for the kickoff meeting (Thursday, 5/6 at 10am PT):
- Confirm primary telemetry sources (app logs, request trace headers, runtime metrics)
- Share any existing dashboards or runbooks you want kept or replaced
- Confirm who will own alert triage on your side (name + pager escalation)

Attachments: Redwood_Onboarding_Itinerary_v1.pdf, dashboard-templates.xlsx, runbook-template.md

Agenda (30 min):
1) Introductions and roles (CS, SRE, App owner) — 5 min
2) Current signal map and gaps — 8 min
3) Quick tour of suggested dashboards & trace hooks — 10 min
4) Action items and owners + next steps — 7 min

Please let me know if the time works. If not, propose two alternatives and we’ll adjust.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Alex Park <alex@skyloftmedia.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Agarwal <pri@skyloftmedia.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary

Sounds good, Laura — 5/6 10am PT works for us.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Telemetry: app logs (structured JSON), tracing via x-request-id propagated from edge -> backend -> model gateway, and Prometheus metrics from the inference pool.
- Dashboards: we have a Grafana org with a few views; I can share links during the call.
- On-call: Priya will be primary triage (pri@skyloftmedia.com), escalate to me on high-severity.

We reviewed the itinerary and attachments briefly — looks good. One ask: can we include a suggested alert threshold for token-latency P95 and for model error-rate (e.g., invalid responses)? Even ballpark numbers would help.

—Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Skyloft Media
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@skyloftmedia.com>, Priya Agarwal <pri@skyloftmedia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary

Alex — great context, thanks. I attached an updated one-pager with example thresholds and a proposed error taxonomy you can edit ahead of the call. High-level guidance (ballpark):
- Token-latency P95: target 300–500ms for interactive endpoints, 700–1200ms for batched async jobs (depends on model).
- Model error-rate (invalid or blank responses): aim <0.5% initially; set a warning at 0.5–1.5% and critical >1.5%.

We'll propose these as starting points and iterate after we see baseline traffic. During the call we’ll also walk through the tracing headers to confirm span stitching.

Marissa and Ben — can you take the call materials below and add any SRE-specific checks (hot path traces, KV cache hit rate, GPU queue depth) before Thursday? Ben, can you also prepare a quick demo of the Redwood model dashboard (5 minutes)?

Thanks — looking forward.

—Laura

[Attachment: Redwood_Onboarding_Itinerary_v1.pdf]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex@skyloftmedia.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary

Adding a couple implementation notes before the call:
- Trace hooks: recommend instrumenting the edge to forward x-request-id and a 3-segment user->service->model span. We'll share a small Node/Go snippet in the meeting chat.
- Alert routing: keep low-cardinality alerts in Skyloft's pager rota; surface platform-level alerts to Redwood only when they indicate degradation beyond retry (we'll include suggested PagerDuty rules).
- Runbooks: use the attached runbook-template.md to establish playbook steps for the three highest severity events (latency spike, model drift, auth failures).

Ben will run the dashboard demo and show the example of prefix/KV cache metrics and the GPU queue depth panel. I added a short SRE checklist link in the agenda doc (see meeting chat).

—Marissa
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex@skyloftmedia.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding kickoff & implementation itinerary

Thanks everyone — short update post prep:

- I recorded a 5-min demo (link in meeting invite) of the model dashboard showing the P95 latency panel, token throughput, KV cache hit rate, and GPU queue depth.
- I prepared two example alert rules we can drop into Skyloft's PagerDuty service:
  * Latency_P95_high: triggers when P95 > 800ms for 5m (warning) and >1200ms for 2m (critical).
  * ModelErrorRate: triggers when error-rate >1.5% for 10m (critical).

- Runbook ownership: suggest Skyloft owns customer-facing runbooks; Redwood will own platform-runbooks and provide a runbook template during handoff.

See you all on Thursday. I'll bring the demo and the PagerDuty JSON snippets.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
